entities.name: Kotlebists – People's Party Our Slovakia
entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
The Kotlebists – People's Party Our Slovakia (ĽSNS) emerged in the context of a growing far-right movement in Slovakia, officially founded in 2009 by Marian Kotleba. The party is headquartered in Banská Bystrica and has its roots in the political and social discontent stemming from the global financial crisis of 2008, which exacerbated nationalistic and anti-establishment sentiments in Eastern Europe. The party's ideology is characterized by Slovak nationalism, social conservatism, and a strong anti-immigrant stance, positioning it within a broader European trend of rising right-wing populism.

The ĽSNS gained significant traction in the 2010s, notably winning 8.04% of the votes in the 2014 European Parliament elections and subsequently securing a place in the National Council of Slovakia in 2016 with over 8% of the vote. Their political activities have included controversial campaigns against Roma communities and the European Union, which they accuse of undermining Slovak sovereignty. The party's rhetoric often invokes historical grievances, drawing on Slovakia's past during World War II and the first Slovak Republic, further polarizing the political landscape within the country.

The legacy of the Kotlebists is marked by their impact on Slovak society and politics, contributing to the normalization of extremist views and the reconfiguration of the political spectrum. Their presence in the National Council has prompted discussions about far-right extremism and its implications for Slovakia's democratic institutions. The party has also inspired similar movements across Eastern Europe, reflecting a wider trend of right-wing populism and nationalistic fervor in response to globalization.
